Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

better adjective and adverb

in quality

also better than, had better, you’d better, it’s better to, there, that’s better!

classical

Hor. S. 1.5.96: postera tempestās melior, via pejor
Liv. 30.30.19: melior tūtiorque est certa pāx quam spērāta victōria

melior, melius

adjective, comparative of bonus (bonus, melior, optimus); genitive meliōris · Declension on Wiktionary

“Better than” is quam or the ablative: quid melius Rōmā?, what is better than Rome? (Ov. Pont. 1.3.37).

Other words

  • melius — better (adverb)

    adverb, comparative of bene (bene, melius, optimē) · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.97: quō melius cēnāret; Traupman 279

  • satius est — it is better to, one had better

    phrase, with an infinitive; often with quam · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 57–58: satius esse crēdō quam metū; Plin. Ep. 1.9.8: satius est enim … ōtiōsum esse quam nihil agere

    The comparative of satis: “more satisfactory, preferable” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • postera tempestās melior, via pejor

    the next day the weather was better, the road worseHor. S. 1.5.96

  • Pudōre et līberālitāte līberōs retinēre satius esse crēdō quam metū.

    I think it better to keep children in hand by a sense of honour and by kindness than by fear.Ter. Ad. 57–58

  • Em, istuc rēctius!

    There, that’s better!Traupman 94

See also I feel better, bad, great.
